title: Underlining the Importance of Peripheral Protic Functional Groups to Enhance the Proton Exchange of Gd-Based MRI Contrast Agents

synthesis.procedure: L1 was prepared by ring-opening of (R)-methyl glycidate with DO3A(tBu)3, followed by TFA/DCM deprotection of the tert-butyl esters and HPLC-MS purification. GdL1 was obtained by dissolving L1 (31 mg, 0.06 mmol) in H2O (1 mL), adding 1 equiv of GdCl3 in H2O (0.2 mL), adjusting the pH to 7 with 0.1 M NaOH, stirring at room temperature overnight, and lyophilizing.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: L1 purified by semipreparative HPLC-MS, converted to HCl salt by two evaporations from 1 M HCl, and freeze-dried. GdL1 isolated by lyophilization; no single-crystal structure reported.
synthesis.yield: L1 75% (62 mg); GdL1 yield not reported

properties.summary: GdL1 is a q=1 HPDO3A-like MRI contrast-agent analogue whose longitudinal relaxivity at pH 7.4 is 4.7 mM−1 s−1 (20 MHz, 25 °C). pH-dependent r1 and NMRD profiles were used to extract proton-exchange and Solomon–Bloembergen–Morgan parameters; the ester analogue lacks the strong acid/base-catalyzed OH proton exchange seen for the carboxylate analogue GdL2.

synthesis.procedure: L2 was obtained by LiOH hydrolysis of the methyl ester of L1(OtBu)3, followed by TFA/DCM deprotection and HPLC-MS purification. GdL2 was prepared from L2 (15 mg, 0.03 mmol) in H2O (1 mL) with 1 equiv of GdCl3 in H2O (0.2 mL); the pH was adjusted to 7 with 0.1 M NaOH, the solution was kept at room temperature overnight, and the complex was lyophilized.

synthesis.temperature: 50 °C for ester hydrolysis (4 h); rt 16 h for TFA deprotection; room temperature overnight for complexation
synthesis.ph: hydrolysis quenched at pH 5; complexation at pH 7.0
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous/methanol hydrolysis; HPLC-MS (Method B); aqueous complexation and lyophilization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After hydrolysis, methanol was removed and the aqueous residue extracted with DCM; L2 was HPLC-purified, converted to the HCl salt, and freeze-dried. GdL2 was isolated by lyophilization. Mononuclear GdL2 itself was not the CCDC-deposited crystal.
synthesis.yield: L2 60% (30 mg); GdL2 yield not reported

properties.summary: Solution GdL2 shows r1 = 5.1 mM−1 s−1 at 20 MHz, 25 °C, pH 7.4. An intramolecular hydrogen bond between the coordinated hydroxyl and the pendant carboxylate enables fast acid- and base-catalyzed proton exchange (kH = 1.5×10^11 M−1 s−1; kOH = 1.7×10^9 M−1 s−1). Thermodynamic stability log K_GdL = 19.26 and dissociation half-life t1/2 = 2.14×10^7 h (pH 7.4, 0.15 M NaCl, 25 °C) were reported. NMRD analysis invoked a small second-sphere water contribution (~0.3 mM−1 s−1 at 20 MHz, 298 K).

synthesis.procedure: The mononuclear complex GdL2 was first prepared from L2 (15 mg, 0.03 mmol) and 1 equiv GdCl3 in water at pH 7 as described for the Gd(III) complexes. Single crystals of formula {[(Gd(H2O)2)2[Gd(L2)H-1(HO-)]2]}·20H2O were then grown by slow evaporation of water from a solution of GdL2 at pH 9.0 in the presence of a slight excess of Gd(OH)3.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow evaporation of water from GdL2 at pH 9 with slight excess Gd(OH)3 afforded triclinic crystals. The asymmetric unit contains one L2 moiety; a crystallographic inversion center generates the tetranuclear dimer, with lattice water filling hydrogen-bonded voids.

properties.summary: Magnetic/relaxometric data in the paper refer to mononuclear solution GdL2 rather than the solid tetranuclear crystal. The structure is a 0D Gd4 dimer with bridging alkoxide and hydroxide and TSAP geometry at the chelated Gd centers.
